title: Practice Test 1
description: A full-length adaptive digital SAT practice test: 98 questions, two modules per section, with an explanation for every question.

questions.passage: Portable video game consoles and wireless speakers tend to contain batteries that can't be easily ______. Environmental policy researcher Jean-Pierre Schweitzer warns that because new batteries can't be put in once the old ones no longer work, the gadgets stop functioning and are usually disposed of as trash.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: New batteries "can't be put in" once old ones fail, so the batteries can't be **replaced**.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Kenneth Grahame's 1908 book *The Wind in the Willows*. The text is about the Mole who is briefly meeting a stranger while traveling with a friend.

[The] Mole stood still a moment, held in thought. As one wakened suddenly from a beautiful dream, who struggles to recall it, and can re-capture nothing but a dim sense of the beauty of it, the beauty! Till that, too, fades away in its turn.
questions.prompt: As used in the text, what does the word "recall" most nearly mean?
questions.explanation: The Mole "struggles to recall" a dream and "can re-capture nothing," so *recall* means **remember**.

questions.passage: There is no doubt that Irving Langmuir must have proved himself to be extraordinarily ______ understanding some of the most advanced concepts in the field of chemistry—in 1932 his remarkable talent and hard work was recognized when he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for "his discoveries and investigations in surface chemistry."
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Langmuir understood advanced concepts and won a Nobel Prize for his "remarkable talent," so he was **adept at** (skilled in) chemistry.

questions.passage: Economists have long observed that firms in related industries tend to cluster in the same area, as is the case in Leeds, UK, where many thread and yarn spinning firms as well as textile weaving firms are located. The factors causing such clustering are ______: what drives firms in certain industries to cluster may not be especially relevant among other industries.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The colon explains that what drives clustering in one industry "may not be especially relevant" in others, so the factors are **variable**.

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Adib Khorram's 2018 novel *Darius the Great Is Not Okay*. Darius, a teenager from the United States, is visiting his grandparents, Babou and Mamou, in Iran. They are preparing for a holiday celebration.

I felt like a tourist. But Babou fussed with my cap a little more, even though Mamou had already gotten it settled. He looked me in the eye from time to time, like he was looking for something, and thought maybe—just maybe—I had it in me after all. Babou hummed to himself as he smoothed out my shoulder seams and rested his hands on them. "I am glad you are here to see this, Darioush-jan." Maybe I wasn't such a tourist.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To demonstrate that Babou and Darius aren't very interested in going to new places
To emphasize that Darius has been looking forward to an event
To suggest that Babou is planning to visit Darius in the United States soon
To show that Babou affects the way Darius thinks of himself
questions.explanation: Darius starts by feeling "like a tourist"; after Babou's attention and kind words he thinks "Maybe I wasn't such a tourist." Babou changes how Darius sees himself.

questions.passage: The food industry has long used thermal technologies to preserve food in large batches. Recent advancements in infrared heating were made through research in Mexico on the preservation of bean flour. Infrared heating is generally considered to be an improvement over more conventional thermal preservation methods: __whereas conventional methods transfer energy from the surface of a food to its interior, infrared heating uses high-intensity infrared light to generate heat within the food itself, thus reducing industrial heating times.__
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole?
choices: It emphasizes the superiority of infrared heating technologies.
It explains why conventional heating methods are popular in commercial applications and proposes a shift away from these methods.
It suggests that there are possible flaws in infrared heating technologies that have not yet been well researched.
It identifies an advantage that infrared heating has over conventional thermal preservation.
questions.explanation: The underlined portion contrasts how the two methods transfer heat and notes that infrared heating reduces heating times, which is an advantage over conventional methods. It doesn't claim overall superiority (A).

questions.passage: In a large community science effort, biologist Abbigail Merrill and colleagues collaborated with hundreds of students and other amateur science enthusiasts for more than three years to study how butterfly color and time of day relate to butterfly behavior. They found that butterfly color might influence behavior more than butterfly size does, and that butterflies were observed to feed more often in the morning than at any other time of day.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Time of day and butterfly color seem to have less influence on butterfly behavior than the location where the butterflies are studied does.
A recent study suggested that butterflies' coloring seems to be less relevant to their behavior than time of day.
Collaboration between professional scientists and members of the public is especially useful when studying the behavior of butterflies and other flying insects.
A large study suggested that butterfly color and time of day might influence the behavior of certain butterflies.
questions.explanation: The study found that butterfly color and time of day may both influence behavior. B reverses the finding about color; A and C aren't discussed.

questions.passage: President Richard Nixon is most famous for his participation in the 1970s Watergate political scandal, a convoluted tale of criminality and eroded ethics involving a constellation of associates such as political operative Jeb Stuart Magruder and Nixon's secretary Rose Mary Woods. But Nixon's legacy is complex: he has been praised for his role in affirming the sovereignty of tribal nations, and he once made an attempt at reforming United States health care policy that is arguably a precursor to the Affordable Care Act, which became law during the Barack Obama administration.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Richard Nixon's reputation is primarily due to the actions of his associates.
Some of Richard Nixon's policies influenced the policies of later administrations.
Jeb Stuart Magruder and Rose Mary Woods were significant figures in the presidency of Richard Nixon.
Richard Nixon is commonly linked with an infamous historical event, but this overshadows some of his notable achievements.
questions.explanation: Nixon is "most famous" for Watergate, "but" his legacy also includes praised achievements (tribal sovereignty, health care reform).

A student is researching those percentages and finds for the marketing year 2012/2013, the percentage of maize exported by ______

Brazil
United States

questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the text?
choices: Brazil exceeded the percentage exported by Argentina for the first time.
Brazil increased from the previous marketing year but remained lower than the percentage exported by the United States.
the United States reached its highest point during the five marketing years.
Argentina decreased from the previous marketing year but remained the highest among the three countries.

questions.passage: A student is writing a research paper on the history of irrigation in the United States, situating the development of Hume Lake (created in Fresno County, California, in 1908) in a larger historical context. The student claims that California's climate renders irrigation an essential component of agriculture in some parts of the state but not in others.
questions.prompt: Which quotation from a study of California agriculture best supports the student's claim?
choices: "The usefulness of irrigation infrastructure in California today cannot be overstated, since it is the most common means of conveying water for agricultural purposes."

"Natural humidity, which renders irrigation unnecessary or reduces its importance in the northern reaches of California, gradually decreases toward the sun-scorched but nonetheless fertile valleys of the southern part of the state."

"Sprinkler irrigation systems are a contemporary way of irrigating that requires machinery to spray water in all directions. These are currently used throughout the United States and are especially prevalent in California."

"The irrigation system developed by the Hohokam people in the 7th century CE, in what is now Arizona, was simple, but this system applied hydraulic engineering design features that are in use today throughout California."
questions.explanation: The claim is that irrigation is essential in some parts of the state but not others. B says irrigation is unnecessary in the humid north but more important in the dry south.

questions.passage: Agricultural scientist Priya Raman tested whether planting clover between rows of corn improves corn yields. During one growing season, she grew corn both with and without clover at three farms. Raman hypothesized that the clover, which adds nitrogen to the soil, would raise corn yields at every farm.

table.title: Corn Yields with and without Clover (bushels per acre)
head: Farm
Without clover
With clover

questions.prompt: Which choice best describes data from the table that support Raman's hypothesis?
choices: At every farm, corn grown with clover yielded more than corn grown without clover.
Farm C had the highest corn yield both with and without clover.
The difference between yields with and without clover was largest at Farm B.
Corn grown without clover yielded at least 148 bushels per acre at every farm.
questions.explanation: The hypothesis predicts higher yields with clover at every farm. A says exactly that (171 > 162, 160 > 148, 179 > 175). B, C, and D are true but don't compare with and without clover at every farm. (This replaces a question that already appears in Practice Test 17.)

questions.passage: Danijel Jug and colleagues found that tilling—the practice of turning soil with hoes, plows, or other machines before planting crops—was associated with an increased yield of winter wheat. But some studies of other crops have found the opposite effect, raising the question of whether the increase in yield found by Jug and colleagues is specific to their study crop. However, it doesn't seem to be the case: ______

table.title: Studies of the Effects of Tilling vs. No Tilling on Crop Yields
head: Authors
Crop
Crop yield with tilling (kilograms per hectare)
Crop yield with no tilling (kilograms per hectare)

questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the assertion?
choices: crop yields with tilling have ranged from 2,693 kilograms per hectare for winter barley to 4,860 kilograms per hectare for winter wheat.
Gevan Behnke and colleagues found a similar association in a study using soybeans.
a study using winter wheat yielded 4,860 kilograms per hectare with tilling and only 3,910 kilograms per hectare without tilling.
R.K. Jat and colleagues reported an even larger positive effect of tilling on the yield of maize.
questions.explanation: To show the effect isn't specific to winter wheat, we need another crop where tilling raised yield. Behnke's soybeans: 4,285 with tilling vs. 3,798 without. Maize (D) and barley went the other way; C is winter wheat again.

questions.passage: J.G. Ballard's 1984 novel *Empire of the Sun* contains elements drawn from Ballard's own life—there are many parallels between the experiences of the novel's protagonist, Jim Graham, and those of Ballard—and as a result *Empire of the Sun* is regularly described as an autobiographical novel. This characterization can be useful, but it also presents drawbacks in terms of how the work is perceived, as it may lead readers to believe that Ballard merely fictionalized true events, which, in an artistic field where creativity and inventiveness are prized, can suggest that Ballard's ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: Ballard should not have claimed that *Empire of the Sun* is based on real events.
the real-world counterparts of other characters in *Empire of the Sun* are hard to identify.
*Empire of the Sun* is less of an imaginative achievement than it actually is.
critics disagree about whether *Empire of the Sun* shows greater originality than works without autobiographical elements.
questions.explanation: If readers think Ballard "merely fictionalized true events" in a field that prizes creativity, they may judge the novel less imaginative than it really is.

questions.passage: All stainless steel contains varying amounts of iron, carbon, and corrosion-inhibiting chromium. However, ferritic stainless steel, often used in induction cookers, contains a higher percentage of chromium (at least 10.5%) than does austenitic stainless steel and a higher concentration of iron, which is responsible for its magnetic properties. Unlike ferritic stainless steel, austenitic stainless steel has a face-centered cubic crystalline structure, which results from the addition of nickel to the alloy. Austenitic stainless steel has two subtypes: the 300 series, often used for aerospace tubing, and the 200 series, which has less nickel and more manganese than the 300 series and is used for dishwashers. Thus, stainless steel used to manufacture ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: aerospace tubing will have similar magnetic properties to stainless steel used to manufacture induction cookers.

both aerospace tubing and dishwashers will have a face-centered cubic crystalline structure, but stainless steel used to manufacture aerospace tubing will have less nickel than stainless steel used to manufacture dishwashers will.
aerospace tubing will have a concentration of manganese greater than 10.5%, while stainless steel used to manufacture dishwashers will not.
aerospace tubing will have less manganese in its composition than stainless steel used to manufacture dishwashers will.
questions.explanation: Aerospace tubing uses the 300 series; dishwashers use the 200 series, which has "more manganese than the 300 series." So tubing steel has less manganese.

questions.passage: In her large-scale sculpture *Casa-Isla*, artist Edra Soto included references to her childhood in Puerto Rico: For example, the sculpture's steel panels have a crisscrossing pattern inspired by the iron gates ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: Soto would see in her neighborhood?
would Soto see in her neighborhood?
would Soto see in her neighborhood.
Soto would see in her neighborhood.
questions.explanation: The sentence is a statement, not a question, so it ends with a period, and the clause keeps normal word order: "Soto would see."

questions.passage: By analyzing the level of radioactive decay within a fossil specimen, scientists can establish the age of that fossil with a high degree of precision. When radioactive elements aren't present, scientists turn to ______ analysis of Earth's sediment layers (strata)—to estimate how old a fossil is based on the age of the strata in which the fossil is found.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The phrase "the analysis of Earth's sediment layers (strata)" is a supplement closed by a dash before "to estimate," so it must open with a dash too.

questions.passage: As an object-oriented computer programming language, Perl is used by coders like Black Girls Code founder Kimberly Bryant ______ programs by manipulating "objects" (that is, specifically defined variables) interacting with each other. Conversely, Pascal, used in software development and educational instruction, is not an object-oriented language.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Is used by coders ... to create programs": the infinitive gives the purpose of using Perl.

questions.passage: Many of the cities and ______ are known by nicknames that correspond to one of their notable features, like landscape, climate, famous residents, or chief exports. For example, the Puerto Rican municipality of Hatillo has also been called "the Blue Coast of Puerto Rico," a nickname that alludes to what the area is well known for: the pristine blue ocean that surrounds it.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: towns, that dot the island of Puerto Rico,
towns that dot the island of Puerto Rico
towns that dot the Island of Puerto Rico,
towns, that dot the island of Puerto Rico
questions.explanation: "That dot the island of Puerto Rico" is essential (it says which towns), so no commas. *Island* isn't part of a proper name here, so it's lowercase.

questions.passage: Anthony van Dyck, a Flemish mannerist painter whose works are distinctive for their precise yet exaggerated details ______ frequently included in the seventeenth-century art movement the Antwerp school, whose members were known for depicting rural life in the Low Countries.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is "Anthony van Dyck" (singular); the long description between commas doesn't change that, so the verb is "is."

questions.passage: Recognized as a National Heritage Area by the United States Congress in 1996, the Rivers of Steel National Heritage Area ______ a region of Pennsylvania that has long been known for its unique natural, cultural, and historical attributes.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The text describes the area as it is now ("has long been known"), so the present tense "is" fits.

questions.passage: As a behavioral economist, Francesca Gino of Harvard Business School examines human economic behavior through a lens that, ______ elements of psychology and economics, illuminates how and why (and to what effect) people make particular choices.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Combining elements of psychology and economics" is a participle phrase between commas inside the clause "a lens that ... illuminates." A finite verb would leave "that" with two verbs.

questions.passage: In his essay "Of Smells," French philosopher Michel de Montaigne explores a relatively light subject, but he addresses heavier fare in "Of the Punishment of Cowardice." Regardless of subject matter, Montaigne works to question his own perspective throughout his essays. ______ his personal motto was "What do I know?"
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Montaigne questions his own perspective, so his motto "What do I know?" is fitting.

questions.passage: The World Cup of men's soccer, one of the biggest sporting events on the planet, brought 32 national teams from six continents to the host country, Brazil, in 2014. The event, which is held every four years, has expanded greatly since it was played in Italy in 1934. ______ the World Cup included only 16 teams, most from Europe and the Americas.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text contrasts 2014 with the 1934 tournament; "Then" moves back to that earlier time.

questions.passage:

• The 1,900-mile journey took forty-one days.

• In 2022, Erick Cedeño, a Black long-distance cyclist, reenacted the journey.
• Cedeño wanted to honor the infantrymen on the journey's 125th anniversary.

The US infantrymen rode their bicycles from Montana to Missouri, traveling a total of 1,900 miles.
The goal of the 1897 journey was to test the idea of forming a military bicycle corps.

choices: To argue that sea otters should be better protected

choices: Daniel decides to sell his grandfather's tools.
Daniel remembers that he never enjoyed working in the workshop.

Students who studied in groups scored higher than students who studied alone.
Most students said they would like to sleep more on school nights.

questions.explanation: $3 + 2k \le 25$ gives $k \le 11$.

questions.prompt: The population of a town is modeled by $P(t) = 1{,}200(1.05)^t$, where $t$ is the number of years after 2020. Which statement is the best interpretation of $1.05$ in this context?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by $1.05$ each year means the population grows by 5% per year.
choices: The population increases by 1.05 people each year.
The population increases by 105% each year.
The population increases by 5% each year.

questions.prompt: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its width, and its perimeter is 64 centimeters. What is the area of the rectangle, in square centimeters?
questions.explanation: $2(3w) + 2w = 64$ gives $w = 8$ and length $24$, so the area is $8 \times 24 = 192$.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 5 red marbles, 7 blue marbles, and 8 green marbles. If one marble is chosen at random, what is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: There are $5 + 8 = 13$ non-blue marbles out of 20.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$3x + 2y = 12$$ $$6x + ky = 24$$ In the given system, $k$ is a constant. For what value of $k$ does the system have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: The second equation must be exactly 2 times the first: $6x + 4y = 24$, so $k = 4$.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: In the equation $x^2 + 6x + c = 0$, $c$ is a constant. If the equation has exactly one real solution, what is the value of $c$?
questions.explanation: Exactly one solution means the discriminant is 0: $36 - 4c = 0$, so $c = 9$.

questions.prompt: In right triangle $PQR$, angle $R$ is the right angle and $\cos P = \dfrac{8}{17}$. What is the value of $\tan Q$?
questions.explanation: Take $PR = 8$ and $PQ = 17$, so $QR = \sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = 15$. From $Q$, the opposite side is $PR$ and the adjacent side is $QR$: $\tan Q = \dfrac{8}{15}$.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $(2x^3)^2 \cdot x^{-2}$, for $x \neq 0$?

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.prompt: In a random sample of 400 voters in a city, 56% supported a new park. The margin of error for this estimate is 4 percentage points. Which conclusion is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: A margin of error gives a plausible range for the whole population: $56 \pm 4$, or 52% to 60%.
choices: Exactly 56% of all voters in the city support the new park.
Fewer than 52% of all voters in the city support the new park.
Between 52% and 60% of the voters in the sample support the new park.
It is plausible that between 52% and 60% of all voters in the city support the new park.

questions.prompt: A circle in the $xy$-plane has the equation $(x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 49$. The point $(2, k)$ lies on the circle, and $k > 0$. What is the value of $k$?
questions.explanation: Substituting $x = 2$: $(k + 3)^2 = 49$, so $k + 3 = \pm 7$, giving $k = 4$ or $k = -10$. Since $k > 0$, $k = 4$.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = a(x - 3)^2 + 5$, where $a$ is a constant. If the graph of $y = f(x)$ passes through the point $(1, 13)$, what is the value of $a$?
Line $k$ is perpendicular to the line $2x + 3y = 7$ and passes through the origin. Which equation represents line $k$?
questions.explanation: The given line has slope $-\dfrac{2}{3}$. A perpendicular line has slope $\dfrac{3}{2}$, and through the origin its intercept is 0.

questions.prompt: If $\dfrac{x}{3} = 7$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by 3: $x = 21$.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: Four notebooks cost \$10. At the same price per notebook, how many dollars do 10 notebooks cost?
questions.explanation: Each notebook costs $10 \div 4 = 2.50$ dollars, and $10 \times 2.50 = 25$.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 2x + 1$. What is the value of $f(5)$?
If $2x + 3 = x + 8$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Subtract $x$ and 3 from both sides: $x = 5$.

questions.prompt: What is 35% of 80?
Which expression is equivalent to $2(3x - 1)$?
questions.explanation: Distribute: $2 \cdot 3x - 2 \cdot 1 = 6x - 2$.

questions.prompt: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points $(1, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$?
A square has a perimeter of 36 centimeters. What is its area, in square centimeters?
questions.explanation: Each side is $36 \div 4 = 9$, so the area is $9^2 = 81$.

questions.prompt: Two angles of a triangle measure $50^\circ$ and $60^\circ$. What is the measure of the third angle?

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: What is the mean of the data set $4, 8, 10, 14$?
questions.explanation: The sum is 36, and $36 \div 4 = 9$.

questions.prompt: A plumber charges a \$50 fee plus \$30 for each hour of work. Which equation gives the total charge $C$, in dollars, for $h$ hours of work?
questions.explanation: The hourly rate multiplies $h$ and the fee is added once: $C = 30h + 50$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $x$ satisfies the inequality $3x - 4 > 11$?
questions.explanation: $3x > 15$, so $x > 5$. Only 6 is greater than 5.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$y = 2x$$ $$x + y = 12$$ If $(x, y)$ is the solution to the given system, what is the value of $y$?
questions.explanation: Substitute: $x + 2x = 12$, so $x = 4$ and $y = 8$.

questions.prompt: A spinner is divided into 8 equal sections, and 3 of the sections are red. What is the probability that the spinner lands on a red section?
questions.explanation: 3 favorable sections out of 8.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: If $x^2 = 49$ and $x > 0$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: $x = \pm 7$, and $x > 0$ gives 7.

questions.prompt: The value $A$, in dollars, of an investment after $t$ years is given by $A = 500(2)^t$. What is the value of the investment after 3 years?
The number of members of a club increased from 50 to 60. By what percent did the number of members increase?
A circle has a radius of 5 centimeters. What is the area of the circle, in square centimeters?
A right triangle has legs of length 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
The line of best fit for a scatterplot is $y = 2.5x + 10$. What $y$-value does the line predict when $x = 8$?
Which expression is equivalent to $x^2 + 5x + 6$?
questions.explanation: Find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5: 2 and 3.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A cyclist rides at a constant speed of 3 meters per second. How many kilometers does the cyclist travel in 1 hour? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.explanation: $3 \times 3{,}600 = 10{,}800$ meters, which is 10.8 kilometers.

questions.prompt: If $3(2x - 5) = 4x + 7$, what is the value of $x$?
The price of an item was decreased by 20%, and then the new price was increased by 25%. The final price is what percent of the original price?
questions.explanation: $0.80 \times 1.25 = 1.00$, so the final price equals the original price.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + k$, where $k$ is a constant. If the minimum value of $f(x)$ is 3, what is the value of $k$?
questions.explanation: The minimum occurs at $x = 2$: $f(2) = 4 - 8 + k = k - 4$. Setting $k - 4 = 3$ gives $k = 7$.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$2x - y = 5$$ $$4x - 2y = c$$ In the given system, $c$ is a constant. For which value of $c$ does the system have infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: The second equation must be exactly 2 times the first, so $c = 2 \times 5 = 10$.

questions.prompt: A right circular cylinder has radius $r$ and height $2r$. If the volume of the cylinder is $54\pi$ cubic units, what is the value of $r$?

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: What is the sum of the solutions to the equation $3x^2 - 12x + 5 = 0$?
questions.explanation: For $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$, the solutions add up to $-\dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{12}{3} = 4$.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: The mean of 5 numbers is 12. When a sixth number is added to the data set, the mean of the 6 numbers is 13. What is the sixth number?
questions.explanation: The first sum is $5 \times 12 = 60$ and the new sum is $6 \times 13 = 78$, so the sixth number is $78 - 60 = 18$.

questions.prompt: Line $\ell$ in the $xy$-plane passes through the points $(2, 5)$ and $(6, 13)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the point on line $\ell$ whose $y$-coordinate is 21?
questions.explanation: The slope is $\dfrac{13 - 5}{6 - 2} = 2$, so $y = 2x + 1$. Setting $2x + 1 = 21$ gives $x = 10$.

questions.prompt: In a circle, a central angle of $72^\circ$ intercepts an arc of length $4\pi$. What is the circumference of the circle?
questions.explanation: $72^\circ$ is $\dfrac{72}{360} = \dfrac{1}{5}$ of the circle, so the circumference is $5 \times 4\pi = 20\pi$.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: If $9^x = 27^{x - 1}$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Write both sides as powers of 3: $3^{2x} = 3^{3x - 3}$, so $2x = 3x - 3$ and $x = 3$.

questions.prompt: The table shows how many students in two grades play a school sport. If a student who does not play a sport is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student is in grade 11?
questions.explanation: Only students who do not play count: $55 + 40 = 95$. Of these, 40 are in grade 11, and $\dfrac{40}{95} = \dfrac{8}{19}$.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which point $(x, y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities $y > 2x - 3$ and $y < -x + 6$?
questions.explanation: For $(1, 2)$: $2 > -1$ and $2 < 5$, so both hold. Each other point fails at least one inequality.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $(x + 3)^2 - (x - 3)^2$?
Triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $DEF$, where $A$ corresponds to $D$ and $B$ corresponds to $E$. If $AB = 6$, $DE = 15$, and the area of triangle $ABC$ is 24, what is the area of triangle $DEF$?
questions.explanation: The scale factor is $\dfrac{15}{6} = 2.5$, so areas scale by $2.5^2 = 6.25$: $24 \times 6.25 = 150$.

questions.prompt: A quantity is 800 at time $t = 0$ and increases by 6% each year. Which equation models the quantity $Q$ after $t$ years?
questions.explanation: A constant percent increase is exponential growth with factor $1 + 0.06 = 1.06$.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: The graphs of $y = x^2 - 4$ and $y = 2x - 1$ intersect at two points. What is the sum of the $x$-coordinates of the two points?
If $\sin(x^\circ) = \cos(40^\circ)$ and $0 < x < 90$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Sine and cosine of complementary angles are equal, so $x = 90 - 40 = 50$.

questions.prompt: A company's cost, in dollars, to produce $n$ items is $C(n) = 1.5n + 240$. Which statement is the best interpretation of $1.5$ in this context?
questions.explanation: $1.5$ is the slope: the change in cost for each additional item.
choices: Each additional item increases the cost by \$1.50.
The company produces 1.5 items per hour.
The cost of producing 240 items is \$1.50.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers surveyed a random sample of 500 students at one university and found that students who reported sleeping more hours had higher grades, on average. Which conclusion is best supported?
questions.explanation: A random sample supports conclusions about that university's students, but an observational survey shows only an association, not cause.
choices: Sleeping more causes students at that university to earn higher grades.
Among students at that university, more sleep is associated with higher grades.
More sleep is associated with higher grades for students at every university.
Sleeping more causes all students everywhere to earn higher grades.

questions.prompt: The height $h$, in meters, of a ball $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by $h(t) = -5t^2 + 20t + 1$. What is the maximum height of the ball, in meters?
A square is inscribed in a circle with radius 5. What is the area of the square?
questions.explanation: The square's diagonal is the circle's diameter, 10. A square with diagonal $d$ has area $\dfrac{d^2}{2} = 50$.

questions.prompt: In the equation $a(x + 2) = 3x + 6$, $a$ is a constant. For what value of $a$ is the equation true for all values of $x$?
questions.explanation: $3x + 6 = 3(x + 2)$, so $a = 3$ makes both sides identical.
